text:
Casey Cizikas is nearing 1,000 NHL games, every one of them as an Islander, which makes him the longest-serving player on the team and one of the rare one-franchise careers left in the league. At 35 he's playing about 12 minutes a night as the fourth-line center, and since the injuries he has had Kyle Palmieri and Simon Holmstrom on his wings.

The points are thin, three in 16 games and one in his last ten, but that's not the job. The Islanders take about 53% of the expected goals with him on the ice, nearly four points better than without him. Evolving-Hockey had opponents getting fewer chances against him last season than against 96% of forwards, which is exactly what you want from a checking center.

Our range has him at 5 to 14 goals over a full season, and he'll probably land near the low end; that's fine. What to watch is the milestone, and the moment it comes in an Islanders sweater at home, it will be one of the better nights of the season on Long Island.
headline: Cizikas, closing in on 1,000
